```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

TOP fits two-stage polytomous logistic regression models for case-control
studies in which cases are characterized by multiple disease or tumor markers.
The recommended interface for new analyses is `top_fit()`.

## Data layout

The outcome matrix has case-control status in its first column (`0` for
controls and `1` for cases) and tumor characteristics in the remaining
columns. Tumor characteristics must be `NA` for controls. If case tumor
characteristics can be missing, use a distinct numeric code and pass it as
`missing_value`.

```{r data}
library(TOP)
data("data", package = "TOP")

y <- data[, 1:5]
snp <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE]
pc1 <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]

head(y)
table(y[, 1])
```

The simulated package data use `888` for missing case tumor characteristics.

## Fit an additive model

Here the SNP and principal component both use an additive second-stage
structure. `top_fit()` validates dimensions, coding, missingness, and finite
covariate values before calling the numerical model.

```{r fit}
fit <- top_fit(
  y = y,
  additive = cbind(snp, pc1),
  missing_value = 888
)

fit
```

Results have stable names. The second-stage table contains baseline
case-control effects and marker-specific case-case effects.

```{r named-results}
fit$second.stage.test
fit$global.test
head(fit$first.stage.test)
```

Standard R methods are also available.

```{r methods}
head(coef(fit, stage = "second"))
dim(vcov(fit, stage = "second"))
summary(fit)
```

## Choose a second-stage structure

Covariates can be assigned to different structures:

- `baseline`: a common association across subtypes;
- `additive`: baseline plus tumor-marker main effects;
- `pairwise`: additive effects plus pairwise marker interactions;
- `saturated`: a separate effect for every retained subtype.

For example, a common SNP effect can be adjusted for an additive PC effect.

```{r mixed-structures, eval=FALSE}
fit_mixed <- top_fit(
  y = y,
  baseline = snp,
  additive = pc1,
  missing_value = 888
)
```

## Subtype counts and convergence

TOP historically omits subtypes with counts at or below the cutoff. The
default `subtype_cutoff = 10` preserves that behavior. Lower cutoffs can make
information matrices unstable, particularly in small datasets. Numerical
failures raise R errors instead of terminating the R session.

Set `options(TOP.verbose = TRUE)` temporarily when EM progress messages are
useful.

## Existing scripts

`TwoStageModel()` remains available for backward compatibility. New code
should prefer `top_fit()` and named components such as
`fit$second.stage.test` rather than positional indexing.
